styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole sign with a small number panel, so per-tile density is judged by eye. Measured: 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue-grey, not black. The sign head shows a lit edge, a face, a number digit and a dark border, and the pole has a highlight and a shadow side. That is about 4 steps against about 5 in the references. Texture is limited to a few rim highlights and the base, with no grain or dots. Next to the richer references (vending-a, kiosk-a) it reads as thinner and simpler, though it is close to the bus-shelter in treatment. A careful artist might accept it as a small sign, but it sits below the standard of the richer references, and when in doubt the verdict is fail.
